Aerial Wildlife Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 303 Aerial Ungulate Survey (2025) 
Background 
WMU 303 is a small unit surrounding Blairmore 
located in southwest, Alberta. It shares the same 
boundaries as the municipality of Crowsnest Pass 
except for the north boundary which follows the 
provincial Forest Reserve boundary. The Crowsnest 
River and Highway 3 both run through it’s center. It 
consists of mountain habitats and the riparian habitat 
created by the Crowsnest river. WMU 303 was also 
surveyed specifically for elk in 2015. Past surveys did 
not calculate population densities or estimates for deer 
species or moose. 
Survey Method 
A rotary wing transect survey was conducted February 
11, 2025 flying 11 east-west lines at 1.85 km intervals, 
with 48 per cent coverage (800 m wide survey strip, 
area surveyed 80.8 km2) for a total linear survey effort 
of 101 km. At each observation point, ungulates were 
classified by species, and when possible, sex and age 
were recorded.  
Moose, deer and elk observations made during the 
survey. Population estimates and confidence 
estimates were not calculated if too few individuals 
were observed. All elk observations were summed for 
a minimum total count.   
Results 
A total of 294 elk were observed with an average 
group size of 73.5 (range 5-219). The bull:cow:calf 
ratio was found to be 13:100:24. The survey results 
are presented in Table 1. The elk population in 2025 is 
92% higher than that reported in 2015. 
The data collected was insufficient to calculate 
population estimates for mule deer (6 seen), white-
tailed deer (36 seen) and moose (1 seen). It is not 
recommended to use the transect method in the future 
to survey WMU 303 for deer and moose. The small 
size, complex shape and presence of several small 
communities resulted in very little data for these 
species.
